## RCA (Phase 1 complete) — confirmed root cause, with the discriminating experiments

### The mechanism, in two parts

**(1) The budget now sits inside the band of legitimate test costs.** Commit `6a5c88027c5`
(story `bold-abeyant-indri`) lowered the per-test hang budget 300 s -> 20 s at
`pyproject.toml:650`, `_build-and-test.yml:662` and `:677`. `git blame -w -C -M` on all three
lines returns `6a5c88027c59` and nothing else; its trailer is `rebar-ticket: 73b8-2d79-3046-44ce`.

The direct PARENT commit `4d6c1cc835e` — same day, same runner class, same
`-n 4 --dist worksteal --cov=rebar`, still on `--timeout=300` — passed clean
(run 32581500417 / job 97051623657: `16182 passed, 66 skipped in 906.38s`, zero crashes) and
its own `--durations=25` block reports fourteen tests between **18.71 s and 29.93 s of `call`
time**, headed by 29.93 s / 28.72 s / 22.97 s / 22.63 s / 22.46 s / 22.44 s / 21.63 s. That list
IS the crash list. So the evidence refuting "20 s is measured, not guessed: the default tier
runs clean at it" was already in CI at the moment the change landed. `timeout_func_only = true`
cannot rescue it: those are `call` times — the test body is the whole-tree scan.

The story's own measurement ("the whole unit tier runs clean at `--timeout=20`, 5097 passed") was
a LOCAL unit-tier run — no `--cov=rebar`, no `tests/scripts`, faster cores. The gating
`ubuntu-latest, py3.13` leg is the only one that adds coverage, and it is the only leg that reds.

**(2) `timeout_method = "thread"` expresses an expiry as a process kill, not as a verdict.**
`pytest_timeout.py:542` (`timeout_timer`) calls `os._exit(1)` from the watchdog thread, so the
xdist worker dies outright. Only the `signal` method reports `Failed: Timeout`, via
`pytest.fail()` at `pytest_timeout.py:502`. **A budget expiry inside an xdist worker can
therefore NEVER print `Failed: Timeout`** — it prints `[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated`
followed by `worker 'gwN' crashed while running '<test>'`.

This resolves the tension the report flagged: the zero `Failed: Timeout` count is a *prediction*
of the mechanism, not evidence against it. Bug `albinic-agrologic-dolphin` (0078-fa3e-05d1-4e12)
independently proved the same mechanism last fortnight, and — pointedly — used
`--timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread` as its deliberate crash-INDUCING amplifier to reproduce a
300 s-budget bug. Story 73b8 then shipped that exact value as the production budget.

### Discriminating experiments (local, worktree off 6a5c88027c5, macOS py3.12)

A probe test with a 25 s body, run under `-n 2 --dist worksteal`:

    ARM A  repo ini as shipped (timeout=20, thread)
           -> [gw0] node down: Not properly terminated
              worker 'gw0' crashed while running '<probe>'
              zero `Failed: Timeout`                      == the CI signature, byte-identical
    ARM B  same 20 s budget, --timeout-method=signal
           -> E  Failed: Timeout (>20.0s) from pytest-timeout.
              1 failed, 1 passed in 20.87s                 worker SURVIVES, clean verdict
    ARM C  pre-73b8 budget, --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread
           -> 2 passed in 25.88s

Arm B isolates the METHOD as what converts a timeout into a worker crash (killing "it is not the
timeout, it is something else"). Arm C isolates the BUDGET as what makes it fire at all (killing
"the thread method was always broken"). Together they leave only: over-tight budget + thread
method = worker crash with no timeout verdict.

Supporting measurement: `--cov=rebar` alone is a ~2x multiplier on these tests locally
(`test_safe_boundary_is_not_unwrapped_in_repository_tests` 2.91 s -> 6.02 s;
`test_gate_reports_no_findings_for_owned_files` 2.01 s -> 4.23 s). The runner's slower cores
under 4-way saturation supply the rest of the gap to 20 s.

### Why it reads as flakiness rather than a hard failure

The budget lands *inside* the cost band, not below it, so which tests die depends on which
marginal test `--dist worksteal` hands to a loaded worker. The crashing set drifts between runs
(`test_reconciler_jira_seam_clean_heldout` in job 97060825782,
`test_residual_drain_seam_clean_heldout` in job 97056277838). And it is self-amplifying: eleven
worker restarts re-pay process + coverage startup, so the suite takes 1057-1077 s instead of
906 s and the SURVIVING scanners are pushed from ~16 s to 19.0-19.95 s — hard against the wall.
Each crash makes the next more likely.

### Pristine main IS affected; change 2098 / story 3436 is NOT implicated

Both failing runs carry headSha `6a5c88027c59d3e24d3e4269838fb3c591a64240`, which is pristine
`origin/main` — no change in flight. Gerrit 2098's revision file list is
`src/rebar/_commands/compact_{txn,rebuild,plan,recovery,trigger}.py`, `compact.py`,
`tests/unit/commands/test_compact_plan.py`, `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_compact_negative.py`
— none of the eleven crashing tests, and neither `pyproject.toml` nor `_build-and-test.yml`.
Main itself is broken for every change; 2098 is collateral.

### Defect legitimacy: `defect` (regression)

Cited authorities: (a) story 73b8's own commit-message claim that the tier "runs clean at" 20 s,
falsified by the parent commit's own CI durations; (b) bug `balsamy-eloquent-iggypops`
(89d5-61da-b621-47f8), which established this guard and sized it at 300 s because "300 s dwarfs
the slowest legitimate test"; (c) bug `albinic-agrologic-dolphin`, whose RCA fixes the meaning of
this exact crash signature; (d) the project's landing rule that a change needs `Verified +1`.

### Attribution

`caused_by` -> **73b8-2d79-3046-44ce** (`bold-abeyant-indri`), introducing commit `6a5c88027c5`.
Clean regression, not an unmet obligation: the implicated lines were CREATED by that commit
(blame returns only it), and the date test agrees — the parent commit ran the same tests clean at
906 s with zero crashes. The link is recorded, and will be passed explicitly as `--caused-by` on
the close so blame auto-derivation cannot add a competing guessed edge.

### Sibling sweep

All `--timeout=` lanes across `.github/workflows/` and the `Makefile`: the two lanes at 20 are
the ONLY ones below 300. The other eleven are 300 / 600 / 900 / 1800 / 3600 — separately
calibrated and all comfortably clear of the 29.93 s worst case. No construct siblings. Parity
census on "where is the per-test budget set": local `pytest` + `make test` (the ini — covered by
the fix), the two shared CI lanes (fixed), the eleven other CI lanes (already >= 300). No MISSING
slot.

# The 20 s per-test hang budget kills xdist workers on every CI run

## Symptom (pristine `origin/main` @ 6a5c88027c5, no other change applied)

Default suite, `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)` — the ONLY leg that adds `--cov=rebar`:

    run 32583448507 / job 97056277838: 11 failed, 16175 passed, 66 skipped in 1077.36s
    run 32585303586 / job 97060825782: 11 failed, 16182 passed, 66 skipped in 1057.20s

Every failure is a worker death, each preceded by `[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated`:

    worker 'gw2' crashed while running 'tests/unit/test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py::test_dropping_a_used_helpers_row_fails_loudly_instead_of_shrinking'
    worker 'gw3' crashed while running 'tests/unit/test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py::test_safe_boundary_is_not_unwrapped_in_repository_tests'
    worker 'gw1' crashed while running 'tests/scripts/test_binding_lifecycle_grace_seam_clean_heldout.py::test_gate_reports_no_findings_whole_tree'
    ... 8 more, all whole-tree scanning gates ...

`grep -c "Failed: Timeout"` = **0** in both jobs. Worker ids run gw0-gw12 under `-n 4`:
xdist replaced each dead worker 11 times. The crashing SET is not stable between runs
(`test_reconciler_jira_seam_clean_heldout` in one, `test_residual_drain_seam_clean_heldout`
in the other), which is why it reads as flakiness.

The integration tier shows the same worker deaths (`node down: Not properly terminated` on
3 of 4 nodes).

## Root cause — CONFIRMED, reproduced deterministically

Commit `6a5c88027c5` (story `bold-abeyant-indri` / 73b8-2d79-3046-44ce) lowered the per-test
hang budget from **300 s to 20 s** in three places: `pyproject.toml:650` (`timeout = 20`, new
`[tool.pytest.ini_options]` keys) and `_build-and-test.yml:662` + `:677`. `git blame -w -C -M`
on all three lines returns `6a5c88027c59` and nothing else.

**Two facts combine.**

1. **~14 legitimate tests genuinely cost more than 20 s on the runner.** The direct PARENT
   commit `4d6c1cc835e`, same day, same runner class, same `-n 4 --dist worksteal --cov=rebar`,
   under the OLD `--timeout=300` (run 32581500417 / job 97051623657, `16182 passed` in 906.38s,
   zero crashes) reports in its own `--durations=25` block:

       29.93s call  test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py::test_safe_boundary_is_not_unwrapped_in_repository_tests
       28.72s call  test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py::test_dropping_a_used_helpers_row_fails_loudly_instead_of_shrinking
       22.97s call  test_binding_lifecycle_grace_seam_clean_heldout.py::test_gate_reports_no_findings_whole_tree
       22.63s call  test_check_config_ownership_heldout.py::test_main_on_real_tree_returns_zero
       22.46s call  test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py::test_gate_reports_no_findings_for_owned_files
       22.44s call  test_cli_seam_clean_heldout.py::test_gate_reports_no_findings_for_owned_files
       21.63s call  test_check_config_ownership_heldout.py::test_real_source_tree_is_clean
       ... 20.87s, 21.24s, 21.29s, 21.42s, 18.71s, 18.76s ...

   That is the crash list. The data refuting "20 s is measured" was in CI at the parent commit.
   These are `call` times, so `timeout_func_only = true` does not help: the body IS the scan.

2. **`timeout_method = "thread"` expresses an expiry as `os._exit(1)`, not as a verdict.**
   `pytest_timeout.py:542` (`timeout_timer`) calls `os._exit(1)` from the watchdog thread,
   killing the xdist worker process outright. Only the `signal` method reports
   `Failed: Timeout`, via `pytest.fail()` at `pytest_timeout.py:502`. So a budget expiry inside
   a worker can NEVER surface as `Failed: Timeout` — it surfaces as `node down` + `worker
   crashed`. The zero `Failed: Timeout` count is a PREDICTION of this mechanism, not evidence
   against it. Bug `albinic-agrologic-dolphin` (0078-fa3e-05d1-4e12) proved this same mechanism
   and used `--timeout=20 --timeout-method=thread` as its deliberate crash-INDUCING amplifier.

**Positive feedback loop:** 11 worker restarts re-pay process + coverage startup, so the suite
runs 1057-1077 s instead of 906 s and the SURVIVING scanners move from ~16 s to 19.0-19.95 s —
right against the wall. Each crash makes the next more likely.

**Local runtime proof** (worktree off 6a5c88027c5, macOS py3.12, three discriminating arms on a
25 s-body probe test under `-n 2 --dist worksteal`):

    ARM A  repo ini (timeout=20, thread)   -> [gw0] node down: Not properly terminated
                                              worker 'gw0' crashed while running '<probe>'
                                              zero `Failed: Timeout`      == the CI signature
    ARM B  same budget, --timeout-method=signal -> `Failed: Timeout (>20.0s) from pytest-timeout.`
                                              a clean verdict, worker survives
    ARM C  pre-73b8 --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread -> 2 passed in 25.88s

Arm B isolates the METHOD as what converts a timeout into a crash; Arm C isolates the BUDGET as
what makes it fire at all. Coverage measured locally as a ~2x multiplier on these tests
(2.91s -> 6.02s), which with the runner's slower cores is the rest of the gap.

## Not attributable to any change in flight

Both failing runs are at headSha `6a5c88027c59d3e24d3e4269838fb3c591a64240` = pristine
`origin/main`. Gerrit change 2098 (story 3436, compact-planner consolidation) touches only
`src/rebar/_commands/compact_*.py` + two compact tests — none of the 11 crashing tests, and
neither config file. It is NOT implicated; main itself is broken for every change.

## Plan

Restore the budget to the value bug `balsamy-eloquent-iggypops` (89d5-61da-b621-47f8)
established and sized ("300s dwarfs the slowest legitimate test"), keeping story 73b8's
genuine improvement — the ini keys, so `make test` and a bare local `pytest` carry the budget
CI does.

1. `pyproject.toml` — `timeout = 20` -> `timeout = 300`, and update the sizing comment to cite
   the measured 29.93 s worst case rather than the falsified "runs clean at 20 s" claim.
2. `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:662` and `:677` — `--timeout=20` -> `--timeout=300`.
   `test_the_shared_tier_lanes_carry_the_ini_timeout_budget` derives from the ini, so it
   follows automatically.
3. `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py` — `_INI_BUDGET_SECS` 20 -> 300, and RESTRUCTURE the
   marker-override arm. It currently proves the override by `time.sleep(budget + 2)` in-tree,
   so its cost is PINNED to the budget: at 300 s it would sleep 302 s. (At 20 s it already
   costs 22.01 s — the single slowest unmarked-equivalent entry in the failing runs.) Move it
   out-of-process onto the same generated-project helper the negative arm already uses, with a
   small generated budget, so the arm costs seconds and the budget is free to be sized on
   evidence instead of on this test's runtime.

`timeout_func_only = true` is deliberately KEPT: it is not implicated in these crashes (the
cost is all `call` time), and dropping it would newly bound local session fixtures — a
behaviour change beyond restoring what broke. Its effect on setup/teardown hang coverage is
recorded as a separate follow-up rather than folded in here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pyproject.toml`'s `[tool.pytest.ini_options].timeout` is 300; checked by
      `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py::test_the_configured_budget_is_the_measured_one`.
- [ ] Both shared-tier lanes in `_build-and-test.yml` run at `--timeout=300`; checked by
      `test_ci_workflow_parity.py::test_the_shared_tier_lanes_carry_the_ini_timeout_budget`.
- [ ] A test whose body outruns the ini budget is still killed by the ini alone; checked by
      the existing negative arm `test_an_unmarked_over_budget_test_is_killed_by_the_ini_alone`.
- [ ] `@pytest.mark.timeout(N, func_only=True)` still overrides the ini; checked by the
      restructured marker-override arm, which must complete in under 30 s regardless of the
      configured budget.
- [ ] The `--timeout-method=thread` hang-guard sweep still passes; checked by
      `test_ci_workflow_parity.py::test_shared_pytest_suite_has_a_per_test_hang_guard`.
- [ ] The ubuntu py3.13 default-suite leg completes with zero `worker '.*' crashed` /
      `node down` lines; checked on the change's own Verified run.

## Verification

    pytest tests/unit/test_timeout_budget.py tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py -q
    pytest tests/scripts -q -n 4 --dist worksteal
